title: Release notes generator: add LTS mode (curated summaries, compatibility + known issues blocks)
author: Devon Price
description: Summary: This PR adds an explicit "--mode=lts" (aka "LTS mode") to the runtime release notes generator. LTS notes are intentionally slower-change and enterprise-friendly: they include curated summaries, a compatibility matrix, and a known-issues block with workarounds. Motivation: Dedicated/Private customers are asking for patch notes that are auditable and predictable (less noisy than mainline changelogs), while still capturing security fixes and operational guidance. This is a prerequisite for cutting the first 1.18.x LTS patch notes from labeled PRs + a small curated input file. Scope: This change is limited to formatting/output + data ingestion for known issues/compat sections. It does not change release tagging, publishing, or any branching logic. Design notes: (1) Input sources: (a) merged PR metadata (title, number, labels, author, merge SHA), (b) a per-release curated YAML file for human-approved summaries (optional overrides), (c) a compatibility matrix YAML (runtime<->driver/cuda/helm/installer), and (d) a known-issues YAML that is maintained by Runtime/SRE. (2) Output: emits both Markdown (customer-facing) and a JSON sidecar used by Console to link sections and render a compact summary. (3) Taxonomy: LTS mode uses a stricter category set (Security, Reliability/Correctness, Performance, Ops/Tooling, Documentation) and suppresses low-signal buckets ("Refactors", "Chores") unless explicitly curated. (4) Safety: generator fails hard if required metadata is missing for Security entries (CVE id or "CVE-PENDING" + tracking link) or if compatibility YAML is inconsistent (unknown GPU/CUDA tuple). Usage: ./tools/release_notes/gen.py --mode=lts --version 1.18.1-lts --base runtime-1.18-lts --since-tag 1.18.0-lts --curation tools/release_notes/curation/1.18.1-lts.yaml --known-issues tools/release_notes/known_issues/lts.yaml --compat tools/release_notes/compat/lts-1.18.yaml. Output files: dist/release-notes/runtime-1.18.1-lts.md and dist/release-notes/runtime-1.18.1-lts.json. Testing: adds golden tests for LTS markdown + JSON output, schema validation for known issues/compat inputs, and unit tests for categorization + gating rules. Follow-ups: (a) wire generator into the release runbook and CI workflow for release/* branches, (b) add an "Upgrade notes" curated section for Private-specific sequencing, (c) allow known issues to be filtered by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) in JSON sidecar.
commits: tools/release_notes: add generator mode flag + dispatcher (gen.py)
add LTS templates (markdown + json sidecar) and taxonomy rules
ingest curated summaries overrides and enforce required fields
add compatibility matrix + known issues schema validators
golden tests for lts output + fixtures for 1.18.1-lts sample
docs: update internal README for release-notes tooling
conversation: Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Can we make the generator fail if an item is labeled security but doesn't include a CVE reference? We need this for the security patch SLA doc. Also please ensure the output includes the exact merge SHA for every entry for auditability.

Devon Price (author): Added required field enforcement: Security items must include CVE or CVE-PENDING + tracking_url in curation YAML; otherwise generator exits non-zero. Also added merge_sha to both markdown table and JSON sidecar for all entries.

Marissa Cole (Product): The notes need a clear top-of-page summary (3–5 bullets) that CS can paste into an email. Can we support a curated "Highlights" section that isn't auto-generated from PR titles?
Devon Price (author): Added optional "highlights" array in curation YAML. If present, it renders as the first section under the header and also maps to JSON.summary for Console/CS reuse.
Jasmine Liu (CS): Known issues block should include workaround + who it affects (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Otherwise Support spends time asking follow-up questions.

Devon Price (author): Added optional fields deployment_modes (Hosted|Dedicated|Private) and workaround. In markdown we show badges for modes. JSON includes modes/workaround fields for Support tooling to consume later.
Paula Mendes (Rollouts/Telemetry): Compatibility matrix should include the Private installer version and Helm chart version, not just CUDA/driver. We link these in Console.

Devon Price (author): Updated compat schema to support private_installer_min/private_installer_rec and helm_chart_min/helm_chart_rec. Template now renders a small matrix with those rows. Added validation that recommended >= minimum.

Elliot Price (Release notes/docs): Template wording: replace "Breaking changes" with "Upgrade notes" for LTS and make it explicit that features may lag mainline. Also please keep the change taxonomy consistent with the Confluence format draft.

Devon Price (author): Renamed section to "Upgrade notes" and added a fixed disclaimer paragraph for LTS. Categories updated to match the draft taxonomy; added a mapping table in README to explain label->category.
Kira Thompson (Runbooks): Can we ensure the output is stable/deterministic (ordering)? Release managers will diff RC vs final and noisy reordering is painful.

Devon Price (author): Sorting rules are now deterministic: category order fixed, entries sorted by (severity desc, PR number asc), and known issues sorted by introduced_version then key. Golden tests cover ordering.
notable_snippet: Example of new CLI usage: `./tools/release_notes/gen.py --mode=lts --version 1.18.1-lts --base runtime-1.18-lts --since-tag 1.18.0-lts --curation tools/release_notes/curation/1.18.1-lts.yaml --known-issues tools/release_notes/known_issues/lts.yaml --compat tools/release_notes/compat/lts-1.18.yaml`
release_notes: Adds LTS-specific release notes templates (Markdown + JSON sidecar)
Supports curated Highlights + per-entry summary overrides for enterprise-friendly notes
Renders Compatibility matrix (CUDA/driver + Private installer + Helm chart expectations)
Renders Known issues block with affected versions, symptoms, workarounds, and deployment modes
Enforces stricter validation for Security entries and schema validation for inputs
